title: Never pull back in an upset | MSFS UPRT guide
description:
Your autopilot just disconnected in heavy MSFS 2024 turbulence—if you pull back on the stick, you will tighten the spiral and overspeed past VMO. Here is how real-world UPRT (Upset Prevention and Recovery Training) saves the aircraft in the Pilatus PC-12 NGX.

Welcome back to Microsoft Flight Simulator A to Z, where U is for UPRT. In MSFS 2024, improved wake turbulence, mountain wave rotors, and rapid icing can push your aircraft past official FAA and EASA upset limits in seconds. In this episode, we jump into the Pilatus PC-12 NGX at 10,000 ft to compare human instinct against real-world recovery procedures on the PFD. You will see why pulling back loads the wing and plunges your vertical speed past 6,000 fpm, how to execute the four-step recovery rule (Push, Roll, Thrust, Stabilize) for both nose-low and nose-high upsets (including underwing jet pitch-up behavior like the Airbus A320), and three simple habits—trim awareness, wake turbulence avoidance, and anti-ice management—that prevent 90% of upsets before they start.

⏱️ Chapters
00:00 - Why pulling back in an upset is fatal
00:49 - Official FAA and EASA upset limits
01:26 - PC-12 NGX live demo: what happens when you pull back
02:03 - Real-world UPRT nose-low recovery (Push, Roll, Thrust, Stabilize)
02:51 - Nose-high upset recovery and A320 thrust pitch-up
03:27 - Three habits to prevent 90% of flight sim upsets
04:02 - The four-word rule and T is for trim
